title: Stream coordination, kernel probing, and snapshot isolation for CUDA graph reliability
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose: Improve correctness and stability of CUDA Graph capture/replay when multiple decode streams interleave prefill and decode phases while also enabling lightweight runtime kernel probing so the runtime can pick the best kernel variant without destabilizing graph replay.

Background: We see rare but production-impacting incidents where a prefill captured on a stream is replayed later with a different kernel variant or KV cache state, leading to subtle output corruption or CUDA errors. Existing mitigations (global mutexes, conservative kernel pinning) either serialize throughput or lose performance on tail latency. This ticket proposes a combined approach: per-stream snapshot isolation for KV/prefix state + ephemeral kernel probing that records kernel fingerprints into the CUDA Graph metadata so replays are compatible.

Scope: Prototype and land a safe design that: (1) creates an epoched snapshot of KV/prefix state at capture time (lightweight epoch ID stored with graph); (2) embeds kernel fingerprints (algorithm+layout+quantization tag) in graph metadata and verifies compatibility on replay; (3) implements a non-blocking stream quiesce/fence that ensures no concurrent prefill modifies the same epoch during capture; (4) adds an opt-in runtime flag for kernel probing that runs short microbenchmarks on first N requests to pick kernel variant, and only updates graph metadata when safe; (5) adds fallback to non-graph decode if verification fails (with metrics & automatic retry).

Proposal details and trade-offs:
- Snapshot isolation: stamp KV state with a monotonic epoch counter on prefill completion. Captured graph references that epoch. Replay verifies current epoch == captured epoch or locates compatible snapshot. Pros: avoids cross-stream contamination. Cons: requires snapshot retention policy and small memory overhead.
- Kernel fingerprints: fingerprint kernel attributes deterministically (op shape, dtype, quantization flags, selected kernel id). On replay, runtime compares fingerprint; mismatch triggers safe fallback or dynamic kernel rebind if binary-compatible.
- Quiesce fence: lightweight per-allocator fence (no global locks) implemented via atomic stream bitsets to wait for outstanding prefill commits that touch same KV shards. This is designed to be low-latency for common cases where conflict is rare.
- Kernel probing: run short probes in a sandboxed context with identical shapes to real requests; limit to first 10 probes per model-version on a node. Recording probes into graph metadata only after two consecutive identical microbench results.

Acceptance criteria:
- No regressions in end-to-end correctness on full decode suites (existing golden prompts + fuzzed interleavings).
- Reduce incidents related to capture/replay mismatches to zero for canary clusters during 2-week canary.
- Measured throughput loss < 2% at p50 and p95 when snapshot isolation is enabled on dedicated pools (bench vs baseline).
- Fallback events should be visible in metrics and have distinct error codes for SRE diagnosis.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/CUDA+Graph+Snapshot+Isolation (draft)
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (WIP)
- Decoding fuzz harness: internal://bench/fuzz/graph-replay-2025-02 (results attached in comments)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge prototype behind feature flag; unit + integration tests green.
2) Canary on dev-dedicated pool (5% traffic) for 2 weeks; monitor graph-fingerprint-mismatch, fallback-rate, p50/p95 latency, and token cost.
3) If stable, enable for dedicated pools with toggle per-customer.

Open questions:
- Snapshot GC: retention policy (time-based vs LRU). Prefer 24-48h default with aggressive LRU for memory pressure.
- How to guarantee compatibility of kernel fingerprint taxonomy across releases? Propose: bump model-runtime ABI and maintain mapper in release notes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Memory pressure from snapshot retention: mitigate with sharded snapshot store and small delta snapshot (only changed KV segments).
- Probing noise: limit probes and require two consecutive consistent results before committing.
- Edge-case race: if replay occurs during snapshot GC, fallback to non-graph path and alert.

Estimated effort: 5 points (design + prototype + tests + canary).

2025-02-03 Jonas Keller (SRE): Observability requirements added: histograms for fallback_reason, graph_fingerprint_mismatch_count, snapshot_gc_pressure. Added ticket ENG-82792 to wire metrics to Datadog.

2025-02-06 Diego Martinez: Implemented kernel fingerprint struct and safe-compare routine. Added conservative fallback path. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892. Please review kernel_fingerprint.h changes.

2025-02-12 Diego Martinez: Patch for shard-id aware quiesce fence pushed. New bench run attached: internal://bench/fuzz/graph-replay-2025-02/results_v2.csv — shows 0 mismatches in 200k interleavings.
